subject: Re: v2.4.0 production deployment rollback - root cause
body:
Hi all,

Following up on this morning's incident: confirmed the prod deploy failed because DATABASE_POOL_SIZE was missing from the new namespace's ConfigMap. The Helm chart pulls this from a values override that was never copied when we cut the new namespace last week.

Sequence of events:
- 09:12 UTC - deploy promoted to prod
- 09:14 UTC - pods enter CrashLoopBackOff
- 09:23 UTC - on-call paged
- 09:35 UTC - rollback completed, service restored

Proposed fix: add a pre-deploy step in the pipeline that diffs required env vars against the target namespace and fails fast. Amanda is drafting the validator script. Will circulate for review before EOD Friday.

Thanks,
Amanda

subject: URGENT: Billing API key exposed in commit 7af3c1e
body:
Team,

Our external secret scanner flagged a commit on the public 'billing-experiments' branch containing a live key for the Stripeworks billing API. The key was pushed at 14:08 and detected at 14:47. The vendor auto-revoked it at 15:12 after our security webhook fired.

Impact assessment so far:
- 2 unauthorized API calls observed in the vendor audit log between 14:50 and 15:05
- Both calls were read-only (GET /accounts), no charges initiated
- Key has been rotated, new key is in the secrets manager only

Next steps:
1. Lena to force-push history rewrite on the branch (in progress)
2. Security to enable mandatory pre-commit secret scanning org-wide
3. Engineering managers to confirm no other developers have local copies of the leaked branch

Please reply with confirmation from your team by tomorrow noon.

- Lena

subject: Re: Re: v2.4.0 production deployment rollback - questions
body:
Amanda,

Thanks for the writeup. Two questions before we sign off:

1. Why did the readiness probe not block promotion? It looks like the probe was returning 200 on the broken pods because the health endpoint didn't exercise the DB pool.
2. Do we have similar values-override gaps in the staging or canary namespaces? If so we should sweep them as part of this fix, not just patch prod.

I'd like the validator script to also assert that staging and canary match prod's env var schema. Happy to review the PR.

Marco

subject: [PR ready] env-var validator for pre-deploy gate
body:
Marco, team,

Validator PR is up: https://git.example.com/devops/deploy-validator/pull/87

Covers both your asks - the script now compares the required env var schema (defined in deploy/required-vars.yaml) against the target namespace's ConfigMap and Secret keys, and fails the pipeline with a clear diff if anything is missing. I ran it against staging and canary and found two unrelated drifts (METRICS_PUSH_URL on canary, FEATURE_FLAG_TTL on staging) - filed cleanup tickets DEVOPS-441 and DEVOPS-442.

Will enable on the prod pipeline once two reviewers approve.

Amanda

subject: Customer export totals don't match - investigation underway
body:
Hi all,

Finance flagged that the monthly customer export shows ~10k rows for the last three months in a row, which is suspiciously round. After digging in, the reporting library we use (pyreportkit 3.4) has a default page size of 10,000 and our wrapper never paginated past the first page. So every export since we upgraded the library in February has been silently truncated.

I'm pulling the affected exports now to quantify the gap. Will follow up with a list of impacted reports and a plan for re-running them.

Raj

subject: Re: Customer export totals don't match - audit impact
body:
Raj,

Thanks for the fast turnaround. From the audit side, three of the truncated exports were used in Q1 board materials. We'll need re-issued versions with a clear note that the original was incomplete. Can you also confirm whether the truncation affected the order of rows, or just the tail end? If it's deterministic by primary key we can at least say the missing rows are predictable.

Let's sync at 3pm if you can.

Dana (Internal Audit)

subject: Resolved: export truncation fix deployed + reissue plan
body:
All,

Fix is live as of this morning - the export job now paginates fully and emits both input and output row counts to our metrics pipeline, with an alert when they diverge by more than 0.1%.

Reissue plan for affected reports:
- 14 reports identified across Jan-Mar 2026
- Reissues will include a banner noting the original was truncated
- Finance-ops to coordinate distribution; ETA EOW

Closing this out. Postmortem doc is in Confluence under /incidents/2026-03-export-truncation.

Raj

subject: Re: URGENT: Billing API key exposed - security confirmations
body:
Lena,

Confirming on the security side:
- Vendor audit log fully retrieved, no further activity beyond the two GETs you noted
- Pre-commit secret scanning hook has been merged into the org-wide template repo (PR #2210)
- Branch protection rule added to require the hook on all repos in the 'billing-*' org group

We still need engineering managers to confirm no local copies of the leaked branch survive. I'll send a follow-up tomorrow if we don't have full confirmation by then.

Elias (Security)

subject: Coordination with Stripeworks vendor security
body:
Hi team,

I got off the call with Stripeworks vendor security. Summary:
- They've confirmed the two unauthorized GETs originated from a Tor exit node
- No data was exfiltrated based on their analysis (response payload was empty for our test account)
- They've offered to issue a written incident attestation for our compliance file
- They've also flagged that their default key TTL is 'never' and recommended we move to short-lived tokens via their OAuth flow

I'd like to add 'migrate billing keys to OAuth' as a follow-up action item. Will file a ticket today.

Lena

subject: Post-incident summary and action items - billing key leak
body:
All,

Closing out the billing key leak incident. Final summary:

Timeline:
- Push: 2026-01-08 14:08 UTC
- Detection: 14:47 UTC (39 min)
- Vendor revocation: 15:12 UTC (1h 4m)
- All clear: 2026-01-10 13:00 UTC

Action items (all owned, dates set):
1. Org-wide pre-commit secret scanning - DONE
2. Migrate billing keys to OAuth short-lived tokens - owner: billing-team, due 2026-02-15
3. Quarterly secret-scan retro - owner: security-team, recurring
4. Update developer onboarding to cover secret handling - owner: people-ops, due 2026-01-31

Thanks to everyone for the fast response.

Lena

subject: Duplicate bug reports in QA - root cause is a stale flag
body:
Hi QA leads,

We've had three duplicate bug reports this sprint about an old experimental layout showing up in QA. Turns out the 'new-cart-experiment' feature flag is still enabled in QA from when we ran the experiment last October. The feature shipped to all users in November and the flag should have been retired.

The original owner (Jamie) left the company in December, and the flag has no current owner in our config. I'll work with the cart team to find a current owner, but more broadly we have no process to detect orphaned flags. Worth a discussion.

Marcus

subject: Proposal: feature flag lifecycle policy
body:
Team,

Following up on the stale flag issue. Proposing the following policy for review:

1. Every feature flag must declare an owner (team, not individual) and an expiration date in the flag config
2. Flags older than 90 days post-launch are auto-flagged for cleanup
3. Flags with no owner team are blocked from being created in CI
4. Quarterly flag audit, owned by platform-team

Draft policy doc: https://wiki.example.com/eng/feature-flag-policy-v1

Would like sign-off from QA, platform, and at least two product engineering teams by end of next week.

Marcus

subject: Failover drill result: read replica was stale
body:
Hi DB and SRE leads,

We ran the planned failover drill on the customer-orders cluster this afternoon. The drill exposed a serious issue: the read replica we promoted was about 19 hours behind the primary due to a replication slot conflict that started on Feb 7. Promotion technically succeeded, but the data was stale enough that order-status queries returned outdated results during the drill window.

This is exactly the failure mode the drill was supposed to catch in advance, but only because we ran it - had this been a real failover we would have served stale data to customers for an unknown duration.

I'm filing a P0 to address replication monitoring gaps. Details to follow.

Sofia

subject: Re: Failover drill - replication slot details
body:
Sofia,

Dug into the slot conflict. Looks like a logical replication slot 'analytics_subscriber' was created on Feb 7 by the analytics team's backfill job and never cleaned up. It accumulated WAL until disk pressure caused our streaming replication to lag. Existing alerts only fired on disk usage above 85%, which never tripped because we have generous headroom.

We need replication-lag-specific alerts at warning (5 min lag) and critical (15 min lag) thresholds. Drafting the alert configs now.

Who should own the conversation with the analytics team about slot hygiene? This will keep happening if backfill jobs don't tear down their slots.

Kenji

subject: Replication monitoring rollout plan
body:
Team,

Monitoring rollout plan for review:

- Warning alert: replication lag > 5 min for 5 consecutive samples (slack to db-team)
- Critical alert: replication lag > 15 min for 3 consecutive samples (page on-call)
- New dashboard: replication lag, WAL retention, slot age - linked from runbook
- Drill cadence change: quarterly instead of annual, drill checklist must include replica freshness verification

Analytics team has agreed to add slot teardown to their backfill job templates. Tracking ticket: DATA-1188.

Please push back if you see issues. Otherwise I'll start the rollout Monday.

Sofia

subject: Drill cadence change is now official
body:
All,

Quick announcement: failover drills are moving from annual to quarterly effective Q2. Calendar invites for the next four drills have been sent to db-team, sre-team, and incident-response. Replica-freshness verification is now part of the drill checklist.

Thanks to everyone who pushed for this after the Feb drill exposed the replication gap.

Sofia

subject: CI builds are crawling - cache poisoning suspected
body:
Hi build-infra,

Builds across the monorepo have been taking 3x as long since Tuesday. I traced it to the shared node_modules cache - a build last week failed mid-install but still wrote a corrupted cache layer under the shared key. Every subsequent build is downloading and partially reinstalling because checksums don't match.

Manually invalidating the cache key now to unblock everyone. But we need to fix the root issue: cache writes from failed builds should be rejected.

Kenji

subject: Cache key fix deployed
body:
All,

Fix is in. Two changes:

1. Cache keys now include a sha256 hash of package-lock.json so cache reuse is exact
2. Cache promotion is gated on build success - failed builds skip the cache write step entirely

Build times are back to baseline (avg 4m12s vs the 12m peak we saw last week). Closing this one out.

Kenji

subject: Identity provider regional outage - downstream impact
body:
All,

Oktaprime is experiencing a 90-minute regional outage in us-east-1 starting around 10:30 UTC. Their JWKS endpoint is returning 503s. As a result, every service in our fleet that verifies JWTs is rejecting valid tokens because we don't cache JWKS keys locally.

Customer impact: ~12% of API traffic is failing auth. We're triaging which services are affected and looking at quick mitigations.

Will update every 30 min.

Priya

subject: Architecture review request: third-party degradation modes
body:
Architecture guild,

Last week's Oktaprime outage exposed a class of risk: we treat several third-party dependencies as if they were never going to fail, with no documented degradation modes. Concrete gaps I can name today:

- JWKS endpoint: no local cache, hard fail on 5xx
- Geocoding API: no cached fallback for repeat queries
- Webhook delivery to Stripeworks: no retry queue, drops on 5xx

Proposing we add 'degradation mode review' as a required gate for any service that integrates a third-party dependency. Would like to discuss at next week's guild meeting.

Priya

subject: JWKS local cache rolled out to all auth services
body:
Team,

Local JWKS caching with a 1h TTL and stale-while-revalidate fallback is now deployed across all 14 services that verify JWTs. Verified behavior in staging by simulating Oktaprime outages with toxiproxy - auth continues to succeed for cached keys with no false rejections.

Closing this incident. Architecture guild action on broader third-party degradation review is tracked separately under ARCH-302.

Priya

subject: Onboarding wiki has a dead VPN gateway listed
body:
Hi IT support,

Three of our new hires this week wasted hours trying to connect through 'vpn-old.corp.example.com' which is what the onboarding wiki lists as the primary gateway. That gateway was decommissioned in August. The current entry point is 'vpn.corp.example.com'.

Updated the wiki page myself but flagging this for two reasons:
1. The decommission ticket from August didn't include a doc update step
2. There's no clear owner of the onboarding wiki, so it stays stale by default

Could we add a quarterly review owner for the onboarding wiki?

Tom

subject: Image processing pods OOM-killed weekly - investigation
body:
Hi media team,

The image-processing worker pods have been OOM-killed roughly once a week for the last two months. We assumed it was load-related, but I pulled the heap dumps and the culprit is clear: thumbnails are being cached in an in-memory dict keyed by image URL, with no eviction. Memory grows ~200MB/day.

This is masked because the OOM kills look identical to regular pod restarts in our dashboards. We're not alerting on OOM specifically.

Will have a fix proposal by end of week.

Elena

subject: Profiling results and proposed fix - thumbnail cache
body:
Team,

Profiling confirmed the leak. Numbers:
- Cache size at 24h uptime: ~5.2GB across ~280k entries
- Cache hit rate: 67% (so the cache is useful, just unbounded)
- Per-entry overhead: ~18KB

Proposed fix:
- Replace the dict with an LRU cache, max 50k entries
- Add a per-entry TTL of 6h (most thumbnails are accessed in bursts)
- Add an OOM-kill-specific Prometheus alert separate from the generic restart alert

Expected steady-state memory: ~900MB. PR is ready for review.

Elena

subject: Image processing memory leak - resolved
body:
All,

LRU cache fix has been live for a week with no OOM kills. Memory is steady at ~870MB per pod (within projection). New OOM-kill alert was tested by deliberately starving a canary pod and fired correctly.

Closing this out. Final note for any team running similar caches: 'a Python dict with no eviction is not a cache, it's a leak.' Updated the platform best-practices doc accordingly.

Elena

subject: The order-processing flaky test isn't actually flaky
body:
Hi payments,

I've been digging into the test_concurrent_charge_dedup test that we've had marked flaky for months. After capturing logs from 30 failed runs, the failure pattern is deterministic: when the test runner schedules the dedup goroutine before the charge-write goroutine, we double-charge. This is a real race condition in production code, not test flakiness.

Given the production duplicate-charge reports from finance over the last quarter, I think this test has been flagging a real bug that we've been retrying past in CI.

Going to file a P0 and would like a payments engineer to pair on the fix.

David

subject: Re: order-processing race condition - triage
body:
David,

Confirmed on our side. The dedup check uses a SELECT-then-INSERT pattern without a unique constraint or transactional locking, so two concurrent charge requests can both pass the dedup check and both write rows. Estimated production impact: ~140 duplicate charges over the past quarter, totaling ~$8.7k that we've been refunding case-by-case via support tickets.

Fix plan:
1. Add a unique constraint on (idempotency_key, customer_id)
2. Convert the dedup check to ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING semantics
3. Backfill the constraint on existing rows (none should violate)

Will have a PR by Friday. Also adding a CI policy to block any PR that increases test retry count without a written justification.

Kofi

subject: Race condition fixed + retry policy update
body:
All,

Fix is in production. Stats since deploy:
- Zero duplicate charges observed (vs ~10/week prior)
- Refund tickets attributable to this issue: zero new ones

Policy change effective today: any PR raising a test's retry count from 1 must include a comment explaining why and link to a tracking ticket for root cause. Lint rule will enforce this in CI.

Thanks David for catching what we'd been ignoring.

Kofi

subject: Restore drill failure: customer-attachments backups broken
body:
All,

Quarterly restore drill ran today on the customer-attachments bucket. Result is bad. The most recent successful backup is 11 days old. The intervening nightly jobs all show 'success' in the orchestrator but the actual S3 destination has no new objects.

Root cause: the IAM credentials used by the backup job rotated on Jan 19 (per our scheduled rotation) but the new credentials were never propagated to the backup runner. The job has been failing silently since then because it logs an upload-skipped error that we don't alert on.

Working with the data-protection team now to see what's recoverable for that 11-day window.

Hana

subject: Customer comms draft - attachments data loss
body:
Comms team,

We've confirmed that ~4,200 customer attachment uploads from Jan 19-30 are unrecoverable. These were uploads to the customer-attachments bucket that bypassed our backup window due to the IAM credential issue I sent on Jan 30.

Draft customer email is in the shared doc: https://docs.example.com/comms/2026-01-attachments-loss-draft

Key points covered:
- Apology and clear scope
- List of affected upload IDs available on request
- Offer to assist with any business impact
- Description of the fix we've put in place

Please review and push back on tone. We want to send by EOW.

Hana

subject: Backup heartbeat monitoring rolled out
body:
Team,

Heartbeat monitoring for backup jobs is live. Mechanics:
- Every backup job publishes a success heartbeat to deadmanssnitch.example.com after each cycle
- Missing heartbeat for one cycle triggers a warning
- Missing for two cycles pages on-call

Applied to all 23 scheduled backup jobs in the catalog. Tested by deliberately disabling one job's credentials in staging - alert fired correctly within 5 min of the missed cycle.

Closing the LL-1011 incident.

Hana

subject: ADR-019 says gRPC-only but we're 60% REST
body:
Architecture guild,

While reviewing a new service design from a junior engineer, I noticed they had picked gRPC because ADR-019 (from 2024) declares it the standard for internal communication. The actual fleet is roughly 40% gRPC and 60% REST. The engineer wasted a week designing around constraints that no longer apply.

Proposing we either:
(a) update ADR-019 to reflect reality with the actual rationale, or
(b) supersede it with a new ADR explaining why we now allow both, with criteria for choosing.

Option (b) is more work but more useful. Thoughts?

Felix

subject: ADR review process - new policy
body:
Guild,

New ADR review process going into effect:

1. Every quarter, ADR owners reconcile their ADR against the service catalog
2. Drift triggers either an update, a new superseding ADR, or an explicit 'accepted drift' note
3. ADRs without a current owner are flagged for re-adoption or retirement
4. New service designs must cite which ADRs they comply with - reviewers verify the cited ADRs are not superseded

ADR-019 specifically is being superseded by ADR-042 (REST/gRPC criteria). Felix is leading.

Grace

subject: Daily exec reports arriving a day late after region migration
body:
Hi reporting-team,

Several exec stakeholders pinged me this morning - the daily KPI report meant for 06:00 local arrived around 30:00 (i.e. next day) for two of our regional VPs. The report job runs in 'local server time' which used to be UTC, but after our datacenter migration last week the new region's local time is UTC+9.

The job itself runs on schedule, but the cutoff window logic uses local time so it's now computing 'yesterday' as a 9-hour-shifted window. Will fix by switching to UTC throughout, but flagging that we likely have other timezone-sensitive jobs with the same shape.

Natalie

subject: UTC-everywhere migration plan for scheduled jobs
body:
Team,

After auditing the scheduled jobs in our pipeline, I found 7 more jobs with the same local-time-cutoff issue. Migration plan:

1. Convert all internal scheduling logic to UTC (8 jobs total including the exec report)
2. Push timezone conversion to the presentation layer only (email subject, file names, in-report timestamps)
3. Add a unit test for each job that asserts cutoff windows are UTC-anchored
4. Document in our scheduled-jobs runbook

ETA two weeks. Will pair with the reporting team on jobs that have user-facing timezone implications.

Natalie

subject: Mobile users blocked - rate limiter rule misfire
body:
All on-call,

We started receiving a flood of customer support tickets from mobile users at 21:30 UTC. Diagnosed within 20 minutes: a new rate-limit rule meant to throttle a scraping bot was applied at /16 CIDR scope instead of /32, which captured an entire mobile carrier's NAT range. About 70 minutes of mobile traffic was rejected before we rolled back the rule.

Rule has been reverted. Doing impact analysis now.

Yusuf

subject: Customer impact analysis - rate-limit incident
body:
Team,

Impact numbers from last night's rate-limit misfire:

- Affected users: ~38,000 (estimated from rejected request count divided by avg req/user)
- Rejected requests: ~2.1M over the 70-minute window
- Customer support tickets so far: 84
- App store reviews mentioning outage: 12
- No revenue impact identified (transactions queued client-side and retried)

Will prepare an internal-only postmortem doc and a customer-facing status page note. Drafting now.

Yusuf

subject: Rate-limit change review process - new gates
body:
Edge team,

New gates for any rate-limit rule change going into effect today:

1. Must be tested in staging with traffic mirroring for at least 30 minutes
2. Must roll out behind a percentage flag (1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%) with observability between steps
3. Must be reviewed by someone other than the author before applying to production
4. CIDR scopes /20 or broader require explicit sign-off from edge-team lead

Policy doc is up at /eng/edge/rate-limit-policy. The policy's lint check is live in our edge config repo.

Yusuf

subject: Q1 access audit - stale admin role on analytics platform
body:
Hi IAM team,

During the Q1 access audit I found that a former contractor (term'd 2025-09-12) still had an admin role assignment on the analytics platform. Last login attributable to the account was 2025-09-08, so likely no actual misuse, but the role survived offboarding by 4 months because role removal was supposed to happen via a manual ticket that nobody filed.

I've revoked the role manually. Filing a P1 to track the broader gap.

Isabella

subject: HR coordination on automated revocation sweep
body:
Hi HR ops,

Following up on the IAM gap from earlier this month. We're building an automated revocation sweep that triggers on offboarding events from the HRIS. To make it work we need:

1. A reliable webhook from your HRIS when a termination is finalized
2. A canonical user identifier we can use to find downstream accounts (employee ID + work email)
3. A daily reconciliation report you can review to catch HRIS data lag

Is there time next week to walk through the integration design? Aiming for production rollout by end of Jan.

Isabella

subject: Automated offboarding revocation is live
body:
All,

Automated revocation sweep deployed. On HRIS termination events, the sweep:

- Disables the user across SSO and 14 integrated platforms within 5 minutes
- Records all role removals to an immutable audit log
- Flags discrepancies (e.g. role exists in a system not in our integration list) for manual review

Tested with two volunteer dummy accounts, both fully revoked within 3 minutes.

Quarterly access reviews will continue as a backstop. Closing LL-1015.

Isabella

subject: Postmortem action items - Q4 2025 metrics
body:
Engineering leadership,

Finished the Q4 postmortem action item retrospective. Numbers are not great:

- 47 action items across 14 postmortems
- 38% had no named owner
- Of the 62% with owners, 60% are still open or have been silently dropped
- 4 of the still-open items relate to incidents that recurred in Q1 2026

Specifically: the 'add JWKS local cache' action from the 2025-08 Oktaprime incident sat unowned. We hit the same root cause again in January (LL-1007).

Proposing a process change. Details in the next email.

Ravi

subject: Postmortem action item tracking - new process
body:
Team,

New process effective immediately:

1. Every postmortem action item must have a named individual owner (not a team) and a due date
2. Items get filed in the same backlog as feature work, with an 'incident-followup' label
3. Engineering leadership reviews open items monthly; items past due trigger an escalation
4. Postmortem cannot be marked 'closed' until all action items have owners and due dates

Dashboard tracking these is at metrics.example.com/incident-followups. First leadership review is April 6.

Ravi

subject: CVE-2026-30412 affects 'reportgen' and we have 140 stale Dependabot PRs
body:
Appsec team,

CVE-2026-30412 in the reportgen library was published yesterday. We're using a vulnerable version in the customer-statements repo. Going to patch, but in the process I noticed that repo has 140 open Dependabot PRs going back nine months. The CODEOWNERS file points to 'team-statements' which was reorganized into 'team-billing-output' last summer.

The upgrade path from our current reportgen version to a patched version is non-trivial because of intermediate breaking changes - what should have been a routine bump is now a multi-week project.

Will triage the most security-relevant PRs first.

Claire

subject: CODEOWNERS validation in CI is live + dep-PR alerting
body:
All,

Two controls deployed:

1. CI now validates that every CODEOWNERS entry resolves to an existing GitHub team or user. PRs that introduce broken owners are blocked.
2. Repos with more than 20 open dependency PRs trigger a weekly digest email to the appsec-team and the listed owners.

The customer-statements repo has been brought current on dependencies. CVE-2026-30412 patch is deployed. Closing LL-1017.

Claire

subject: Capacity test predicted headroom but prod saturated NAT gateway
body:
Performance team,

Last month's capacity load test predicted comfortable headroom at 3x current peak. Yesterday's traffic spike (1.8x peak) saturated an internal NAT gateway and we shed traffic for 11 minutes.

Reason: the load test environment has direct VPC peering with no NAT in the egress path, while production goes through a NAT gateway for internal-to-internal calls due to historical IP allowlist requirements with our payments vendor. The NAT gateway has a per-source-port connection limit we never modeled.

The load test was technically valid for the environment we ran it in - it just wasn't representative of production.

Oliver

subject: Load test environment parity - what changed and what's tracked
body:
Team,

Load test environment now mirrors production network topology including:
- NAT gateway in egress path (with same connection limits)
- Egress proxies for third-party calls
- Inter-AZ link bandwidth caps matching production

Known-difference list (will appear in every load test report):
- Database is 1/4 the size of production (cost reasons; documented impact in test reports)
- Cache cluster has 3 nodes vs 9 in production

These remaining gaps are tracked as known risks. Re-ran the capacity test on the updated environment - new headroom estimate is 1.4x peak, much closer to the real saturation point we hit. Capacity planning has been notified.

Oliver

subject: Sev-2 incident - on-call didn't see escalating alerts due to batching
body:
Incident-response,

During tonight's Sev-2 (search latency spike, 23 min impact) the responder didn't see the early warning alerts because our notification system batches alerts on a 15-minute interval. By the time the digest landed, customer impact had already begun. Without the batching delay we would have caught this 11 minutes earlier.

Incident retro is scheduled for Wednesday but I want to file the alerting fix now, separately from any other followups.

Amir

subject: Alerting batching fix deployed
body:
Team,

Notification routing has been updated. Changes:

- Incident-class alerts (P0, P1, P2) bypass batching entirely
- Routine/info alerts retain the 15-min batch for noise reduction
- Notification rules added to the quarterly incident drill checklist

Validated by triggering synthetic Sev-2 alerts in staging - delivery latency is now under 30 seconds. Closing LL-1019.

Amir

subject: DR drill retro - runbook drift caused 40-min RTO miss
body:
All,

We just wrapped the DR exercise responding to the regional cloud provider degradation. Headline: we recovered, but RTO targets were missed by 40 minutes because the documented runbook pointed to a vendor admin console that was retired in their migration last fall. Three different URLs in the runbook were stale.

The responders improvised, found the new console paths, and continued, but this is exactly the kind of drift a real DR event will magnify.

Proposing:
1. End-to-end DR runbook drills at least twice per year, with a real responder following the doc verbatim
2. Any deviation found during a drill triggers an immediate runbook update before the drill is closed
3. Vendor migration notices get a checklist item to scrub all runbooks for affected URLs/paths

Full retro doc: https://wiki.example.com/dr/2026-01-retro

Grace
